records.title: Topics in Population Bioethics
records.header: B H 201 Topics in Population Bioethics (2) SSc
records.text: B H 201 Topics in Population Bioethics (2) SSc Introduces students to bioethical questions that arise in public health, population health, and global health, situating ethical questions and challenges within a broader social context and perspective. Students interact in a small-scale learning environment with classmates and faculty and have the opportunity to learn more about the Bioethics Minor. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Ethical Issues in Modern Medicine
records.header: B H 311 Ethical Issues in Modern Medicine (3) SSc
records.text: B H 311 Ethical Issues in Modern Medicine (3) SSc Case-based approach to ethical topics in medicine, such as abortion, genetic testing, physician-assisted death, and euthanasia. Emphasizes utilizing ethical principles and methods of case analysis. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Bioethics: Secular and Jewish Perspectives
records.header: B H 339 Bioethics: Secular and Jewish Perspectives (3) SSc, DIV
records.text: B H 339 Bioethics: Secular and Jewish Perspectives (3) SSc, DIV Legal, ethical, scientific, and Jewish religious perspectives on contemporary medical and biomedical research practices. Legal and civil rights of women, people with disabilities, minors and minority or marginalized groups. Key differences between secular and Biblical/Rabbinic approaches in interpretation, analysis and application of bioethics, doctor-patient relationships; reproductive methods; abortion; euthanasia; and stem cell research. Offered: jointly with JEW ST 339/MELC 328.

records.title: Ethical Theory
records.text: B H 402 Ethical Theory (5) SSc Studies the major normative ethical theories, including both teleological and deontological approaches. Emphasizes moral philosophy during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, as well as contemporary commentary. Offered: jointly with PHIL 412.

records.title: Metaethical Theory
records.text: B H 404 Metaethical Theory (5) SSc Studies the major metaethical theories, including both cognitivist and noncognitivist approaches. Emphasizes moral philosophy during the twentieth century, as well as contemporary commentary. Offered: jointly with PHIL 413.

records.title: Ethics and the Social Determinants of Health
records.header: B H 409 Ethics and the Social Determinants of Health (3) SSc, DIV
records.text: B H 409 Ethics and the Social Determinants of Health (3) SSc, DIV Examines ethical issues confronting healthcare workers caring for poor & minority populations, whose capacity for health and recovery from disease are compromised by social conditions in which they grow up, live, work, and age. Aims to broaden/reorient understandings of disease, patient autonomy, and clinician duties within contexts of structural inequalities related to socioeconomic status/race/ethnicity/gender/other salient social differences. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Philosophical Problems in Bioethics
records.header: B H 420 Philosophical Problems in Bioethics (3) SSc
records.text: B H 420 Philosophical Problems in Bioethics (3) SSc Introduces the philosophical concepts and controversies that underlie contemporary bioethical debates. Explores issues using the literature of bioethics and philosophy, contemporary film, works of fiction, and conversations with health professionals. Students learn philosophical methods of analysis and argument, and debate different sides of ethical issues.

records.title: History of Eugenics
records.header: B H 421 History of Eugenics (5) SSc
records.text: B H 421 History of Eugenics (5) SSc Examines the history of ideas, policies, and practices associated with eugenics and human genetics from the late nineteenth century to the present in American society and other national contexts. Offered: jointly with DIS ST 421.

records.title: Epidemics and the Politics of Blame: Eugenic and Racial Logics in Shaping U.S. Health Policy
records.header: B H 430 Epidemics and the Politics of Blame: Eugenic and Racial Logics in Shaping U.S. Health Policy (5) DIV
records.text: B H 430 Epidemics and the Politics of Blame: Eugenic and Racial Logics in Shaping U.S. Health Policy (5) DIV Explores the role of narrative in the construction and circulation of scientific and social notions of risk, disease, and contagion, and how these notions are linked to enduring lines of social inequality. Students develop a critical understanding of the relationship between social inequality, medical knowledge, and policy. Recommended: coursework in either bioethics and humanities, sociology, or public health. Offered: W.

records.title: Philosophy of Medicine
records.header: B H 440 Philosophy of Medicine (5) SSc
records.text: B H 440 Philosophy of Medicine (5) SSc Familiarizes students with central issues in the philosophy of medicine. Focuses on the nature of medical knowledge, the connection between theory and observation, the meaning of medical concepts, and the relationship between theories and the world. Offered: jointly with PHIL 459.

records.text: B H 444 Ethical Implications of Emerging Biotechnology (3) Introduces students to select biotechnology innovations and invites consideration of the ethical and policy implications surrounding their development and potential use. Offered: W.

records.title: Social Justice and Health
records.header: B H 456 Social Justice and Health (5) SSc
records.text: B H 456 Social Justice and Health (5) SSc Examines the moral grounds for the view that social inequalities in health are unjust using contemporary literature from moral philosophy and bioethics, case studies, and film. Explores basic questions integral to determinations of social injustice as well as moral constraints on the pursuit of health equity.

records.header: B H 460 Reflections on Research, Responsibility, and Society (3) SSc
records.text: B H 460 Reflections on Research, Responsibility, and Society (3) SSc Explores ethical and policy issues that emerge in the conduct of basic, applied, translational, community-based, and collaborative research. Addresses the ethical debates that arise in the context of planning, implementing, and disseminating research.

records.title: Justice in Health Care
records.header: B H 474 Justice in Health Care (5) SSc/A&H
records.text: B H 474 Justice in Health Care (5) SSc/A&H Examination of the ethical problem of allocating scarce medical resources. Emphasizes the fundamental principles of justice that support alternative health policies. Offered: jointly with PHIL 411.

records.title: Racism and the Institution of Medicine: Racial Knowledge, Professional Power, and Black Health
records.header: B H 481 Racism and the Institution of Medicine: Racial Knowledge, Professional Power, and Black Health (3) SSc, DIV
records.text: B H 481 Racism and the Institution of Medicine: Racial Knowledge, Professional Power, and Black Health (3) SSc, DIV Covers the historical provenance of the move to find and account for racial differences in health. Students develop a critical understanding of the impact of the transatlantic slave trade on the contemporary production of medical knowledge and health inequities. Recommended: a social science or humanities course focused on social inequality. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Global Perspectives in Bioethics
records.header: B H 488 Global Perspectives in Bioethics (3) SSc, DIV
records.text: B H 488 Global Perspectives in Bioethics (3) SSc, DIV Examines problems in bioethics from diverse global standpoints, including East Asian, Sub-Saharran African and Western. Our emphasis is on developing a deeper understanding of the cultural assumptions that lie just beneath the surface of bioethics debates. Readings from contemporary philosophy, film and literature. Recommended: prior coursework in ethics, philosophy, or global health. Offered: jointly with G H 419; W.
